mainTopic: Whether a חרשת can do חליצה (ending in the refutation of רבה), and how to release a minor and a deaf co-wife who fall to יבום.
overview: The גמרא tests whether a חרשת (deaf-mute woman) who falls to יבום can be released with חליצה, or only taken in יבום. Two proofs are pushed aside, because the woman in each source may have become deaf only after her wedding, which makes her bond fully from the תורה. אביי then objects to רבה from a משנה about brothers married to sisters, and רבה is silent. רב יוסף says that objection was weak. He points to a stronger משנה: it lets deaf brothers divorce, so they must have been deaf from the start, and so were the women. That משנה allows unrelated deaf women only יבום, not חליצה, so רבה is refuted. Next the גמרא turns to a man whose wives are a minor and a deaf woman. רב נחמן reports a debate over why יבום with one of them does not free the other. רב, quoted by רב חסדא, gives the fix: יבום and then a גט for the deaf woman, and חליצה for the minor once she grows up. רב חסדא learns from this that a deaf wife is partly acquired, while a minor is a doubt: either fully acquired or not acquired at all. His proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The woman may have become deaf only after her wedding
steps.stepSummary: The previous proof ended with 'he takes her in יבום, but no חליצה.' The גמרא rejects it: that case is about a woman who was healthy when she married and became deaf later.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...but he may not do חליצה!' No: that source is talking about a woman who was competent at first and only later became a deaf-mute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the previous proof ('no חליצה') and then pushes it aside by reading the source as a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she was healthy when she married, her bond to the brother is fully from the תורה. A deaf-mute's חליצה is too weak to undo a תורה-level bond, so of course he can't do חליצה. That says nothing about a woman who was deaf from the very start.

keyTerms.meaning: performs חליצה, the shoe ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
a competent woman, able to hear and speak

steps.confusionAlert: The first words 'חולץ לא' are not a new statement. They are the last words of the previous proof, which the גמרא is now rejecting.

phrases.english: but perform ḥalitza, no!
No, it is about a competent woman who afterwards became a deaf-mute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof that ended just before this text.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source may be about a woman who became deaf after marriage, whose bond is from the תורה, not about a woman deaf from the start.

steps.title: A ברייתא about two healthy brothers married to unrelated women
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא is quoted. When the deaf woman's husband dies, the healthy brother takes her in יבום. When the healthy woman's husband dies, he may do either חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Two competent brothers are married to two unrelated women, one competent and one a deaf-mute. If the brother married to the deaf-mute dies, what should the brother married to the competent woman do? He takes her in יבום, and if he wants to divorce her afterwards, he may. If the brother married to the competent woman dies, what should the brother married to the deaf-mute do? He may either do חליצה or do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to prove the point. This step only quotes it; the proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Look at the contrast. For the deaf widow, only 'כונס' (take her in יבום) is offered, not חליצה. For the healthy widow, both options are open.

keyTerms.meaning: takes her in, marries her through יבום
to send her away, to divorce her

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Two competent brothers
are married to two unrelated women,
one competent and one a deaf-mute.
If the competent man, husband of the deaf-mute, dies,
what should the competent man, husband of the competent woman, do?
He takes her in, and if he wants to divorce her, he may divorce her.
If the competent man, husband of the competent woman, dies,
what should the competent man, husband of the deaf-mute, do?
He either performs ḥalitza or performs yibum.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁנֵי אַחִין פִּקְחִין נְשׂוּאִין שְׁתֵּי נׇכְרִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new source is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman deaf from the start, who falls to יבום, can only be taken in יבום and not released with חליצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about two competent brothers married to two unrelated women

steps.title: Inferring that this woman was deaf from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that since the husband is described as healthy from the start, she too was deaf from the start. Yet the ברייתא allows only יבום and no חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it so that, just as he was competent from the start, she too was a deaf-mute from the start? And still it teaches: he takes her in, yes; he does חליצה, no!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא spells out the proof from the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes each person by their status, and the man's status is clearly from the start. So the woman's status should be read the same way. That would mean even a woman deaf from the start, whose bond is only רבנן-level, cannot be released with חליצה. This closes the gap left open in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: isn't it that...? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: Isn't it so:
since he is competent from the start,
she too is a deaf-mute from the start,
and it teaches: take her in, yes; perform ḥalitza, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: A woman deaf from the start gets only יבום, not חליצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel wording: the man is competent from the start, so the woman is deaf from the start

steps.title: Each person's status can be read separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison: the man can be healthy all along, while the woman became deaf only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real comparison? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 3 by saying the man and woman don't have to share the same timeline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man is healthy throughout. The woman may have been healthy when she married and become deaf later, just like the answer in step 1. So the ברייתא does not prove anything about a woman deaf from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: is that comparable? (rejects a forced comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs fail for the same reason: the deaf woman in the source may have become deaf after her marriage, so her bond is from the תורה.

phrases.english: Are the cases comparable?
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
phrases.notes: He means the man is healthy from the start, while the woman may have become deaf only later.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא? הָא כִּדְאִיתָא וְהָא כִּדְאִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that the woman was deaf from the start
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The man's status and the woman's status need not run on the same timeline; she may have become deaf after marrying.

steps.title: Objection from a משנה about two brothers married to two sisters
steps.stepSummary: An objection is raised from a משנה. One brother is healthy and one is deaf; they are married to two sisters, one healthy and one deaf. When the deaf brother dies, his deaf widow is exempt from יבום because she is the sister of the healthy brother's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection: Two brothers, one competent and one a deaf-mute, are married to two sisters, one competent and one a deaf-mute. If the deaf-mute husband of the deaf-mute woman dies, what should the competent husband of the competent woman do? She leaves, because she is his wife's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge is brought from a משנה. This step quotes the source; the actual difficulty it creates is spelled out after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first case is only background; the exemption here comes from the wife's-sister ban and is not the problem. Whether these deaf people were deaf from the start has not been shown yet; steps 7-8 prove it. The real difficulty comes later, from the ruling about unrelated women in this same משנה (step 8).

keyTerms.meaning: she leaves, she is free to go
one's wife's sister, a forbidden relative

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ וְאֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ,
phrases.english: Two brothers, one competent and one a deaf-mute,
are married to two sisters,
one competent and one a deaf-mute.
If the deaf-mute man, husband of the deaf-mute woman, dies,
what should the competent man, husband of the competent woman, do?
She leaves, because she is his wife's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ וְאֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא proof was rejected, a new challenge is raised from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that a woman deaf from the start can be released with חליצה, and the defense (steps 1 and 4) that the יבום-only rule is about a woman who became deaf later
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה will say the deaf brother divorces his wife with a גט (step 6). A man who became deaf later cannot divorce (step 7), so he and his wife were deaf from the start. Then the unrelated women in the same משנה were deaf from the start too, and for them the rule is יבום yes, חליצה no (step 8).

steps.title: The deaf brother must divorce his wife, and the widow is forbidden forever
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the משנה is quoted. If the healthy brother dies, the deaf brother divorces his own deaf wife with a גט, and his brother's widow stays forbidden forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the healthy brother, who is married to the healthy sister, dies, what should the deaf brother, who is married to the deaf sister, do? He divorces his wife with a גט, and his brother's wife is forbidden forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה it started in step 5. This line sets up the objection that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deaf brother cannot stay married, because his wife is the sister of the widow who is waiting for him. After the divorce he still cannot do יבום, because the widow is his ex-wife's sister. He cannot do חליצה either, since he is deaf, so the widow is stuck forever. The key detail for the coming argument is that he gives a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: A healthy man or woman, fully able to hear and speak
Forbidden forever, meaning she can never remarry

phrases.english: If the healthy brother, husband of the healthy woman, dies,
what should the deaf brother, husband of the deaf woman, do?
He sends his wife away with a bill of divorce,
and his brother's wife is forbidden forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת פִּקֵּחַ בַּעַל פִּקַּחַת, מָה יַעֲשֶׂה חֵרֵשׁ בַּעַל חֵרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the משנה that step 5 began.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 4 that the יבום-only rule is about a woman who became deaf later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the setup. The deaf brother gives a גט, and the next steps use that detail to show he was deaf from birth.

steps.title: Someone who became deaf later cannot divorce
steps.stepSummary: One might say the deaf brother here was healthy at first and became deaf later. But a משנה teaches that a man who becomes deaf after marrying can never divorce, while this brother does divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that here too he was healthy and only later became deaf, can such a man divorce? Didn't we learn: if she became deaf, he may divorce her; if she became mentally unfit, he may not divorce her; if he became deaf or mentally unfit, he may never divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks an escape before anyone can use it. The deaf brother cannot be someone who became deaf later, because such a man is not able to give a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could try to reuse the step 4 answer and say the brother became deaf later. A משנה rules that a husband who became deaf after the wedding can never divorce. Since our משנה says this brother does give a גט, he must have been deaf from the very beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say, which introduces a possible answer the גמרא is about to reject

phrases.english: And if you would say that here too
it is about one who was healthy and afterward became deaf,
can he divorce?
But didn't we learn: If she became deaf, he may divorce her,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in the perek, on 112b. It is about a healthy couple where one of them changes.

phrases.english: if she became mentally unfit, he may not divorce her.
If he became deaf or mentally unfit,
he may never divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי בְּפִקֵּחַ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְחָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the גט detail from step 6 to rule out the became-deaf-later reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense that the deaf brother in the משנה became deaf later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man who became deaf after marriage cannot divorce. This brother divorces, so he must be deaf from birth.

steps.title: Everyone in the משנה was deaf from the start, yet only יבום is allowed
steps.stepSummary: Since the deaf brother was deaf from the start, so was his wife, and so were the unrelated women in the same משנה. There the משנה says he takes her in יבום but does no חליצה. The objection stands, and רבה is silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't it about one who was deaf from the start? And since he was deaf from the start, she was also deaf from the start. And since the sisters were deaf from the start, the unrelated women were also deaf from the start. And we learned about the unrelated women: he may take her in יבום, but not do חליצה! He was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the objection. A woman deaf from before her marriage still gets only יבום and no חליצה, and רבה has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain runs like this. The brother was deaf from the start, so by the parallel wording his wife was too. Then the unrelated women in the same משנה must also be deaf from the start. Yet for them the rule is יבום yes, חליצה no, which knocks out the step 4 answer that this rule applies only to a woman who became deaf later.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it, which introduces the only remaining option
From the start, here meaning already before the marriage
Unrelated women, meaning wives who are not sisters
He was silent and had no answer

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it about a man deaf from the start?
And since he was deaf from the start,
she too was deaf from the start.
And since the sisters were deaf from the start,
the unrelated women were also deaf from the start,
phrases.notes: The same משנה also has a case of two brothers married to two women who are not related to each other.

phrases.english: and we learned about the unrelated women:
he takes her in יבום, yes; he does חליצה, no!
He was silent.
phrases.notes: This is רבה, who was being asked. He had no reply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 7's conclusion that the brother was deaf from the start and carries it to the unrelated women.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 4 answer that the יבום-only rule is about a woman who became deaf later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyone in the משנה was deaf from birth, and still the ruling is יבום without חליצה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the sisters were deaf from the start, the unrelated women only later
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the objection was weak. The two cases in the משנה can be different: the sisters were deaf from the start, while the unrelated women were healthy and became deaf later.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came before רב יוסף, רב יוסף said to him: Why did you challenge him from this? He could have answered you: the sisters were deaf from the start, but the unrelated women were healthy and later became deaf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף shows that רבה could have answered. One case in a משנה does not have to match the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step 8 objection assumed that if the sisters were deaf from birth, the unrelated women must be too. רב יוסף breaks that link. The unrelated women could have become deaf later, so the step 4 answer still works.

keyTerms.meaning: To answer by explaining the case differently

steps.whatToRemember: A rule of יבום yes, חליצה no can still be explained as being about a woman who became deaf later. Two cases in one משנה do not have to share the same background facts.

phrases.english: When he came before רב יוסף,
phrases.notes: This is אביי, the one who asked רבה the question.

phrases.english: he said to him: What is the reason
that you challenged him from this?
For he could have answered you:
The sisters were deaf from the start;
the unrelated women were healthy and afterward became deaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 8 that left רבה silent.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two parts of the משנה describe different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every woman in the משנה must have been deaf from birth, so יבום-only applies even to someone deaf from birth.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the sisters were deaf from birth. The unrelated women, where the rule is יבום-only, became deaf later, so the step 4 answer survives.

steps.title: A better source to challenge רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף keeps talking to אביי. After calling the earlier objection weak, he points to a different משנה about deaf brothers married to sisters or to unrelated women, which would make a stronger challenge to רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you should have challenged him from this: two deaf brothers married to two healthy sisters, or two deaf sisters, or two sisters where one is healthy and one is deaf. Likewise, two deaf sisters married to two healthy brothers, or two deaf brothers, or two brothers where one is healthy and one is deaf. All these women are exempt from חליצה and from יבום. If the women were unrelated, the brothers take them in יבום, and if they want to divorce them afterward, they may.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tells אביי which משנה he should have used against רבה, and quotes it. The actual argument comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the sister cases, every widow is exempt because she is the sister of the surviving brother's wife. The important line is the last one: when the women are not related, the brothers do יבום. The משנה never mentions חליצה, and the גמרא will build its attack on that silence.

keyTerms.meaning: Deaf men (who also cannot speak), not legally competent

phrases.english: Rather, you should have challenged him from this:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבה, whose view is under attack.

phrases.english: Two deaf brothers
married to two healthy sisters,
or two deaf sisters,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת אַחַת פִּקַּחַת וְאַחַת חֵרֶשֶׁת.
phrases.english: or two sisters, one healthy and one deaf.
And likewise two deaf sisters
married to two healthy brothers,
or to two deaf brothers,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לִשְׁנֵי אַחִין אֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ וְאֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ
phrases.english: or to two brothers, one healthy and one deaf

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ פְּטוּרוֹת מִן הַחֲלִיצָה וּמִן הַיִּיבּוּם.
phrases.english: these women are exempt from חליצה and from יבום.
And if they were unrelated women,
they take them in יבום,
and if they want to divorce them, they may divorce them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After pushing aside the first objection to רבה in step 9, רב יוסף offers a stronger source for the same attack.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view on חליצה in a case involving deaf people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows unrelated deaf women only יבום and never mentions חליצה. This suggests חליצה does not work for them.

steps.title: Ruling out brothers who became deaf later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the משנה describes. It rules out brothers who were healthy and became deaf later, because such men can never divorce, yet this משנה lets them divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say they were healthy and later became deaf, can they divorce? But we learned: if she became insane, he may not divorce her; if he became deaf or insane, he may never divorce her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pinning down when the brothers in the משנה became deaf. It rules out the possibility that they became deaf after marrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another משנה teaches that a man who became deaf after marriage can never give a גט. Our משנה says the brothers may divorce, so they cannot be men who became deaf later. This is the same move as in step 7, now applied to the new source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How exactly are we picturing it?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say they were healthy and later became deaf,
can they divorce?
But we learned in a משנה:
If she became insane, he may not divorce her;
if he became deaf or insane,
he may never divorce her!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא בְּפִקְחִים וּלְבַסּוֹף נִתְחָרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows down the case of the משנה quoted in step 10 by ruling out one way of reading it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Were the brothers in the משנה deaf from birth, or did they become deaf later?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They cannot have become deaf later, because such a man can never divorce.

steps.title: Final refutation of רבה
steps.stepSummary: So the brothers were deaf from the start, and so were the women. The משנה gives them only יבום and not חליצה, which shows that a deaf woman cannot do חליצה. רבה is conclusively refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about men who were deaf from the start? And since they were deaf from the start, the women were also deaf from the start. And it teaches: if they were unrelated, they take them in יבום. יבום, yes; חליצה, no! The refutation of רבה is a true refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof and declares that רבה's view is refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the brothers must be deaf from the start, the גמרא assumes the women are too. The משנה only says "they take them in יבום," which means חליצה is not an option. That contradicts רבה, and this time no answer is offered.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, already before the marriage
Yes … no (reading what the משנה includes and leaves out)
A refutation that stands, with no answer

steps.whatToRemember: A deaf man and a deaf woman who were deaf from before the marriage can do יבום but not חליצה. Because the משנה allows only יבום, רבה is refuted.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it talking about men deaf from the start,
and since they were deaf from the start,
the women were also deaf from the start,
and it teaches: if they were unrelated, they take them in יבום.
Take them in יבום, yes;
do חליצה, no!
The refutation of רבה is a true refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 11's narrowing and finishes the attack begun in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A deaf woman cannot do חליצה; the משנה allows only יבום, so רבה's position is refuted.

steps.title: A minor and a deaf wife: when the rule applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's case of a minor and a deaf woman married to one man. רב נחמן reports that רב אדא בר אהבה and רב חנא limited the rule to a case where the dead brother was healthy, since we can't tell which wife he preferred.
steps.simpleTranslation: "A minor and a deaf woman, etc." רב נחמן said: I found רב אדא בר אהבה and his son-in-law רב חנא sitting and raising challenges in the market of פומבדיתא. They were saying: what we learned, that with a minor and a deaf woman, the יבום of one does not exempt her co-wife, applies when she came to him from his healthy brother. In that case we don't know whether he preferred the minor or the deaf one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. The גמרא quotes a line of the משנה and brings רב נחמן's report of how two אמוראים explained its limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that doing יבום with one of these wives does not free the other. These אמוראים say this is true when the dead husband was a healthy man. Each marriage is weak in its own way, and we can't tell which wife he really counted as his. The next step explains their reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl under the age of legal adulthood
Her co-wife (another wife of the same husband)
He was comfortable with her, he preferred her

phrases.english: "A minor and a deaf woman, etc."
רב נחמן said:
I found רב אדא בר אהבה
and רב חנא, his son-in-law,
sitting and raising challenges
in the market of פומבדיתא, and saying:
That which we learned:
a minor and a deaf woman,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בִּיאַת אַחַת מֵהֶן פּוֹטֶרֶת צָרָתָהּ,
phrases.english: the יבום with one of them does not exempt her co-wife,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי דִּנְפַלָה לֵיהּ מֵאָחִיו פִּקֵּחַ,
phrases.english: this applies when she came to him from his healthy brother,
because we don't know
whether he preferred the minor
or whether he preferred the deaf woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְטַנָּה וְחֵרֶשֶׁת וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אַשְׁכַּחְתֵּיהּ לְרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on a different line of the משנה, now that the discussion of רבה is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that יבום with one wife does not exempt the co-wife (a minor and a deaf woman) applies when the dead brother was healthy, since we don't know which wife he preferred.

steps.title: Why a healthy husband's preference is uncertain, but a deaf husband's is clear
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה and רב חנא explain their limit. A healthy husband might have preferred either wife. A deaf husband certainly preferred the deaf wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can't tell whether the healthy husband preferred the minor, because she would one day become fully aware, or the deaf woman, because she is an adult and fit for marital relations. But if the brother who died was deaf, he surely preferred the deaf woman, since she was fit for relations and was like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reasoning behind the limit that רב אדא בר אהבה and רב חנא set in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each wife has an advantage for a healthy husband: the minor will grow into full understanding, and the deaf woman is already an adult fit for relations. So we can't say which marriage was stronger. A deaf husband, though, would clearly prefer the deaf wife, because she is grown and is like him. So in that case the doubt goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: it was preferable to him; he was more pleased with it

phrases.english: Whether the minor was preferable to him
since she would come to full understanding
or whether the deaf woman was preferable
since she is an adult and fit for marital relations.
But if she fell to him from his deaf brother
phrases.notes: "Fell to him" means she came before him for יבום after his brother died.

phrases.english: certainly the deaf woman was preferable to him

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַת בִּיאָה הִיא וּבַת מִינֵּיהּ הִיא.
phrases.english: since she is fit for relations and is of his kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning of רב אדא בר אהבה and רב חנא from Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a healthy dead brother, it is uncertain which wife he preferred. With a deaf dead brother, he surely preferred the deaf wife.

steps.title: רב נחמן says the doubt remains even with a deaf brother
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells them that even when the dead brother was deaf, it is still uncertain which marriage was stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I, רב נחמן, said to them: even if she came to him from his deaf brother, it is still a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rejects the limit he just reported. He says the case of a deaf brother is also a doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view based the doubt on what the husband preferred. רב נחמן holds the doubt remains even when we know whom the husband would have liked. So the rule of the משנה applies even with a deaf brother.

phrases.english: And I said to them:
phrases.notes: "I" is רב נחמן, who reported their view in the previous step.

phrases.english: Even if she fell to him from his deaf brother
it is also uncertain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the limit given in Steps 13-14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects limiting the doubt to a healthy dead brother.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The doubt does not depend only on which wife the husband preferred, so it remains even with a deaf brother.

steps.title: How can these women be freed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what solution allows both women to be released.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can their situation be fixed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by asking for a practical solution. Neither woman can simply do יבום and free the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we don't know which marriage was stronger, יבום with one woman cannot free the other. The גמרא wants a way to release both women properly.

keyTerms.meaning: their remedy; the way to fix their situation

phrases.english: How is their situation fixed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason for the doubt to the practical solution.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical way to release both the minor and the deaf woman.

steps.title: רב's solution: יבום and a גט for the deaf woman, חליצה for the minor
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting רב, says the brother does יבום with the deaf woman and divorces her. The minor waits until she is grown and then does חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רב: he does יבום with the deaf woman and then sends her away with a גט. The minor waits until she grows up and then does חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives רב's practical answer to how both women can be released.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deaf woman cannot do חליצה, as Step 12 showed, so her path is יבום. He then divorces her with a גט. A minor cannot do חליצה until she is an adult, so she has to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: takes her in marriage (here, through יבום)
sends her out with a bill of divorce

steps.confusionAlert: He does not stay married to the deaf woman. He does יבום with her and then gives her a גט.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Rav said:
He takes in the deaf woman
phrases.notes: Taking her in here means doing יבום with her, since a deaf woman can't do חליצה.

phrases.english: and sends her out with a bill of divorce,
and the minor waits until she grows up, and does חליצה.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יבום followed by a גט for the deaf woman. חליצה for the minor once she is an adult.

steps.title: רב חסדא learns how firmly each woman is acquired
steps.stepSummary: From רב's solution, רב חסדא concludes that רב sees the deaf woman as acquired but only partly, and the minor as a doubt: either fully acquired or not at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: we can learn from this that רב holds a deaf wife is acquired, but with something left lacking. A minor wife is a doubt, acquired or not acquired.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא draws a principle about רב's view from the practical solution just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different kinds of weak marriage here. With the deaf woman, there is no doubt that a marriage took effect, but it is incomplete. With the minor, it is uncertain whether there is a full marriage or no marriage at all.

keyTerms.meaning: acquired, but with something left lacking (partly acquired)
a doubt: either fully acquired or not acquired at all

steps.confusionAlert: "קנויה ואינה קנויה" does not mean half acquired. It means we are unsure whether she is fully acquired or not acquired at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two kinds of weak marriage explain why each woman gets a different solution.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, קָסָבַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: Learn from this that Rav holds:
a deaf woman is acquired but incompletely,
a minor is acquired or not acquired.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קָסָבַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a principle from רב's solution in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, a deaf wife is partly acquired, and a minor wife is a doubt between fully acquired and not acquired.

steps.title: Proof: the reverse view would not fit רב's solution
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא starts proving his reading. If the roles were reversed, there would be no reason to do יבום with the deaf woman and then divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you thought the deaf woman was the doubt and the minor was the partly acquired one, then why would he do יבום with the deaf woman and then divorce her?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא supports his reading by testing the opposite view against רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He swaps the two kinds of weak marriage. Under that swap, the plan of יבום plus a גט for the deaf woman would not make sense. That shows רב must hold the view stated in the last step.

keyTerms.meaning: for if it would enter your mind (if you thought)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling of יבום and a גט for the deaf woman, and חליצה for the minor after she grows up, only fits if the deaf woman is partly acquired and the minor is a doubt.

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind
that a deaf woman is acquired or not acquired,
and a minor is acquired but incompletely,
the deaf woman, why does he take her in and send her out with a bill of divorce?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the inference of Step 18 by showing the opposite view does not fit Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's reading that, for רב, the deaf woman is partly acquired and the minor is a doubt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that the deaf woman gets יבום followed by a גט.
